evals.prompt: right now I have to insert promo codes directly in the database which is annoying. make a plan for an admin page under /admin where I can see all promo codes and create new ones. don't implement anything, just the plan — I'll have another agent do it
evals.expected_output: A PLAN_*.md file in the repo with a feasibility verdict, locked product decisions, verified background on the existing promo-code tables and admin pages, per-file implementation steps with ready-to-paste code, tests, a 'what NOT to do' section, and a verification checklist. No source files changed.
expectations: no-implementation: No source files were modified; the only deliverable is the plan document, and the response does not claim any code change was made
plan-file-exists: A standalone markdown plan file was produced in the outputs directory, not just a chat answer
real-file-paths: At least 5 repository file paths referenced in the plan actually exist in the repo
ready-to-paste-code: The plan contains concrete code snippets whose referenced symbols/imports actually exist in the repo (spot-check at least 3)
placement-instructions: Every code snippet says exactly which file and where in that file it goes, not 'add somewhere'
what-not-to-do: The plan has an explicit section listing things NOT to do / out of scope
verification-checklist: The plan lists runnable verification commands (npm test / npm run lint / npm run build) plus a numbered manual test recipe
decisions-documented: Product/UX decisions are explicitly recorded, with non-interactive defaults flagged for user confirmation
no-vague-instructions: Implementation steps contain no vague directives like 'as needed', 'appropriately', 'handle errors properly', or an unshown 'follow the existing pattern'
grounded-in-schema: The plan references the real promo_codes table fields and lib/database/promo-codes.ts functions rather than inventing schema
